html.body: Date: 2025-03-25 REMARKSFavorable reconsideration of this Application, in light of the following discussion, is respectfully requested. Claims 1-7 were originally presented. Claims 1-2 and 7 have been amended, and no new claims have been added. Accordingly, claims 1-7 are pending in the present Application. Applicant submits that upon entry of the present Response, claims 1-7 are in condition for allowance. Moreover, the Applicant submits that no new matter has been introduced by the foregoing amendments.Allowable Subject Matter The outstanding Office Action indicates that claims 1-4 and 7 are objected to as being dependent on a rejected base claim but would be allowable if rewritten or amended to overcome the rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), 2nd paragraph, set forth in the Office action.Applicant acknowledges with appreciation the indication of allowable subject matter. In response, the claims are amended consistent with the outstanding Action and the Examiner interview noted below.Examiner Interview First, Applicant wishes to thank the Examiner for the courtesy of an interview granted to Applicant's representative on March 4, 2025, at which time the outstanding issues in this case were discussed. Arguments similar to the ones developed hereinafter were presented and the Examiner indicated that in light of the arguments, he would reconsider the outstanding grounds for rejection upon formal submission of a response.Claim Objections In the outstanding Office Action, claim 1 is objected to because of informalities. However, Applicant respectfully submits that, since the "one end of the belt-like body" is firstly recited in line 8, it is necessary to recite that "one end of the belt-like body in a longitudinal direction", so as to define which direction's end the one end is. Furthermore, "along a direction intersecting the belt-like body" is intended as a modifier not for the "region" but for "attached". Thus, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the claim objection in view of this discussion.Rejections under 35 U.S.C. §112 In the outstanding Office Action, claims 1-4 and 7 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph as being indefinite.In response to the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, the claims are amended to correct the noted informalities. In view of the amended claims , it is believed that all pending claims are definite and no further rejection on that basis is anticipated. If, however, the Examiner disagrees, the Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned who will be happy to work with the Examiner in a joint effort to derive mutually acceptable language.CONCLUSIONConsequently, in view of the present amendment and in light of the above discussion, the outstanding grounds of rejection are believed to have been overcome. The Application, as amended, is believed to be in condition of allowance. An early and favorable action to that effect is respectfully requested.Respectfully submitted, /Timothy J.
